text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The EU cartell has asked the Austrian government to explain the consequences by mid-January of a possible takeover of bank Creditanstalt by Bank Austria.
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said dissolving the coalition between the Social Democrats and conservative People's Party would be "absolutely wrong and would be no use to anybody."
- Finance chief of the postal system, former economics minister Johannes Ditz, is grooming the post for flotation with a complete restructuring to find new sources of income.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank has moved into the Romanian market by setting up a branch office with a base capital of 122 million schillings, Bucharest newspapers report.

- Construction firm Universale is expected to pay out a higher dividend for 1996 thanks to the effects from a dramatic restructuring programme. Pre-tax profit for 1996 is expected to come in at around 20 to 50 million schillings.
- Austrian industry sees turnover growing by a real 2.5 percent in 1997, according to an economic survey.
- Sara Lee/Douwe Egberts is moving into the Austrian coffee market with the takeover of Santora, a producer of coffee beans, drinking chocolate, tea and sugar.
- Austrians drank 20 percent more sparkling wine in 1996 than in the year before, mainly due to lower prices.

- The coalition government is concerned about reaching agreement on the contentious sale of Creditanstalt. Conservative People's Party head Wolfgang Schuessel said about the possibility the sale would not go ahead before year-end: "Better no decision, than a wrong decision."
- Editorial says decision over Creditanstalt sale to fall today. If again no decision is made, then international financial markets will react negatively.
